clue.text: Happening to turn to friend at last

parts.note: a happening is an event, an occurrence
U stands for a turn, as in a U-turn
a friend or supporter is an ally

explanation.surface: Something happens and someone finally turns to a friend for help.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end, and 'to' is just a link between the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean finally, after a long wait or delay.

clue.text: Old hands putting chopped-up tree into transporters

indicators.note: putting one thing into another tells us to place the shuffled letters inside a container word

parts.note: vans are vehicles that transport goods

indicators.note: a tree that is chopped up is cut into pieces, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Logs from a felled tree are being loaded into delivery lorries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped-up' turns TREE into ETER, which goes 'into' VANS.
explanation.definitionFit: An old hand is an experienced person, and veterans are people with long experience.

clue.text: Be agreeably sleepy?

parts.note: one small movement of the head both shows agreement and is what a drowsy person does when dropping off

explanation.definitionFit: To bob the head signals assent, and to doze off in a chair is to drop the head too.

clue.text: Employment? Give us time!

parts.note: taken as written
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A busy worker, asked to take on a job, pleads for more time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give' is only a link; the definition 'Employment' is the noun use, as in the use of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the way something is used, its employment or application.

clue.text: Mary's pet leading girl a dance

indicators.note: one piece leading another means it comes in front of it

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme 'Mary had a little lamb', the lamb is Mary's pet
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl called Mary's pet leads another girl in a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mary's pet' points to the nursery rhyme 'Mary had a little lamb'.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast Brazilian dance for couples.

clue.text: From here Roy takes flight with wild shriek

indicators.note: letters that take flight scatter, so the name is rearranged
something wild is disordered, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A man named Roy runs off screaming wildly from his home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes flight' turns ROY into YOR and 'wild' turns SHRIEK into KSHIRE. 'From' is a link, and 'here' stands for the place Roy comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A place-word: the clue treats the English county as the spot Roy hails from, a large county in northern England.

clue.text: Apple core consumed by head

indicators.note: the core of an apple is its centre, so take the middle letter of the word

parts.note: consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Someone eats the core of an apple, swallowing it head and all.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of APPLE is P; 'by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pate is an old word for the top of the head, the crown.

clue.text: Large old case said to have several uses

definitions.meaning: a large travelling trunk that opens into two halves, now old-fashioned
a word blending the forms and meanings of two others, like smog, is called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: A big hinged travelling bag, and also a term from Lewis Carroll for a blended word that carries two meanings at once.

clue.text: Sensation felt when metal leg breaks?

parts.note: tin is a metal

indicators.note: a leg that breaks is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stinging feeling comes when a metal leg snaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' turns LEG into GLE; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tingle is a prickling or stinging sensation on the skin.

clue.text: Good breeding expected of tenants here

definitions.text: Good breeding expected of tenants here

parts.words: Good breeding expected of tenants here
parts.note: the tenants are horses kept for mating, so good breeding means reproduction, not manners

explanation.definitionFit: A farm where stallions and mares are kept so that fine horses can be bred.

clue.text: Agog, on receiving phone message from god

indicators.note: the phone message comes from the god, so the god comes first

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
a ring is a phone call, as in give me a ring

explanation.surface: Someone is eager on getting a phone call from a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on receiving' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone keen and impatient to start, as in raring to go.

clue.text: Abandoned, did he curse miserably about love?

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes about, around, the letter for love
cursing miserably suggests the word is twisted into a new order

parts.note: O is love, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A castaway, left alone on an island, swears in misery about lost love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miserably' turns CURSE into CRUSE, which goes 'about' O.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's fictional hero, the castaway shipwrecked alone on an island for many years.

clue.text: Device to make one calm after a ghost appears?

indicators.note: calm comes after the ghost, so it is the second piece

parts.note: a ghost is a spirit
level means calm and steady, as in level-headed

explanation.surface: Someone frightened by a ghost needs something to steady their nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make one' and 'appears' are links; the tool uses a bubble in liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder's tool with an air bubble in liquid that shows whether a surface is horizontal.

clue.text: Synod may bless Babel

indicators.note: the Tower of Babel brought confusion of tongues, so these letters are confused

explanation.surface: A church council might bless the Tower of Babel.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is a church council, a formal gathering of clergy.

clue.text: Foreboding of panic stations — ship lost — wrecked, I accepted

indicators.note: a wrecked thing is smashed apart, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the ship is lost, so its letters drop out of the phrase

parts.note: SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: Panic stations as a ship goes down, with the speaker taken aboard the rescue boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes SS from PANIC STATIONS, leaving PANICTATION; 'accepted' adds I, and 'wrecked' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Anticipation is expectation of what is to come, and a foreboding is a fearful expectation.

clue.text: Greatly inspired by the printed word?

definitions.text: Greatly inspired by the printed word?

parts.words: Greatly inspired by the printed word
parts.note: the word for being struck with admiration also means stamped or printed, as type is pressed onto paper

explanation.definitionFit: Admiring and moved, and also pressed or stamped, the way print is laid on paper.

clue.text: Pete less agile but Jack can climb them

indicators.note: agile means nimble and moving freely, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Pete is less nimble, but his friend Jack can scale tall church towers.
explanation.walkthrough: A steeplejack climbs tall structures to repair them, so Jack is the worker, not a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplejack is a workman who climbs church spires and tall chimneys.

clue.text: Show clearly, chaps in swirling mist are making better progress

definitions.note: the plural answer stands for advances, so a singular noun phrase covers it loosely

indicators.note: the chaps and the proof go in the swirling mist, inside its letters
swirling mist moves around, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to prove is to show clearly
chaps means men

explanation.surface: Men are proving themselves by advancing through a swirling mist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show clearly' reads like a command but is the verb to prove; 'swirling' scrambles the mist, and 'in' puts the other pieces inside it. 'are making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvements are advances, changes for the better.

clue.text: Former students' remedy is incomprehensible

parts.note: OBs are old boys, former students of a school
a remedy is a cure

explanation.surface: A remedy favoured by old boys of a school is beyond understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure means hard to understand, unclear.

clue.text: Issue conceived as controversial by Rome?

indicators.note: something controversial is disputed, so these letters are turned about

explanation.surface: Rome regards an issue as a controversial one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means offspring, not a matter for debate; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is offspring conceived but not yet born.

clue.text: Fish return south to find metal-extracting plants

parts.note: a smelt is a small fish
read as re-turn: RE, meaning about, turned round gives ER

explanation.surface: Fish swim back south and find factories that process ore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' is split as RE + turn, so the RE is turned to give ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Smelters are works that melt ore to get the metal out.

clue.text: Petulant-looking pigeon?

definitions.meaning: one who sulks, pushing the lips out in a sulky way
a breed of domestic pigeon able to puff out its crop

explanation.definitionFit: A sulky person who pushes the lips forward, and a breed of pigeon that inflates its crop.

clue.text: Parking fine the monarch declared to be stiff

parts.note: P stands for parking on road signs
OK means fine, all right
ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A parking fine is declared by the monarch to be rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declared to be' is only a link; 'stiff' refers to a fireside rod, as stiff as a poker.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker is a stiff metal rod for stirring a fire, the type of rigidity in as stiff as a poker.

clue.text: Poet in the churchyard?

definitions.meaning: Robert ..., the English poet and novelist

explanation.definitionFit: Robert Graves wrote I, Claudius and war poetry, and churchyards are full of burial plots.

clue.text: Relatives settled in Lundy eccentric, and far from friendly

indicators.note: the relatives have settled in the island, so they go inside its letters
eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Relations who moved to Lundy, a small island off Devon, became odd and hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: Lundy is a small island in the Bristol Channel, off Devon; 'eccentric' scrambles its name and 'settled in' puts the relatives inside. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkindly means in an unfriendly or harsh way.

clue.text: A religious palindrome

indicators.note: the clue says the answer reads the same backwards as forwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a woman in a religious order, and religious is a noun for a monk or nun.

clue.text: Frustrate with a blunt weapon

definitions.meaning: to thwart or prevent someone's plans
a fencing sword with a button on its tip

explanation.definitionFit: To thwart a plan, and a light fencing sword with a blunted point.

clue.text: Diners are sampling starter badly cooked: gloom apparent!

indicators.note: a dish badly cooked is a mess, so these letters are jumbled
the starter of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Diners trying a poorly made first course feel gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly cooked' turns DINERS ARE into DREARINES, and 'starter' gives the S of 'sampling'; 'apparent' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreariness is dullness and depressing gloom.
